oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the

condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The most structurally transferable context, flupenthixol (a tricyclic antipsychotic with a basic side chain), has absolute oral bioavailability values of 30–70%, 55%, 40%, and 48%, all above the 20% threshold; L2 adds a tabulated 40% and a 1.51-fold increase for oral films.

Other basic-amine/piperazine and sulfone-containing reference drugs with F ≥20% include vilazodone (72% fed), trazodone (63–91% and 65±6%), imidafenacin (57.8% human), and odanacatib (49% fed with high-fat meal).

L3 trazodone oral exposure records show substantial Cmax (~1.6 µg/mL) and AUC (~10 µg·h/mL) after 100 mg oral, consistent with the high absolute bioavailability in the same context; these exposure records are not direct F measurements but reinforce the high direction.

L5 gut-wall efflux and intestinal-metabolism records concern other molecules (fexofenadine, domperidone, sulpiride, carbamazepine, asimadoline, florfenicol, ebastine) and provide no query-specific evidence; they do not affirmatively support F <20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule is available in the supplied records.
No matched oral versus IV exposure data exist for the exact query structure.
No query-specific gut-wall efflux or intestinal metabolism data are provided; L5 records are for other molecules and some conflict (e.g., domperidone efflux ratio <2 vs 3.32).
No query-specific intestinal permeability, solubility, or dissolution measurement is provided.
Transfer from flupenthixol and trazodone is structural/contextual; the methylsulfonyl and carboxamide substituents may alter absorption, but this is not affirmative evidence for F <20%.
